en.html:
The sky had looked suspicious since morning, and by near noon it finally showed its true nature. Fat raindrops were pounding the garden soil, determined to wipe out the results of daily careful upkeep.

Thunder reached my ears too. Still distant, but coming closer little by little.

Heaven's uproar, however, was hollow, and no use at all for stopping my mind from sinking into gloomy thought. And there was no one to talk to.

The Chief was out at work. Makimura, the <ruby>steward<rt>steward</rt></ruby>, was busy. Muramasa also was away on her daily Silver Star search. Rain interferes with a sword-armor's detection function, but her ability to catch the Silver Star's <ruby>scent<rt>presence</rt></ruby> is a separate matter, so apparently there is no problem.

A sword-armor that knows no rust will not suffer in the rain, I suppose. I thought of my partner in her spider form, flying about dark Kamakura and throwing off water drops, and I envied her. With something to be done, one is spared pointless brooding.

...I had been fighting. Fighting, fighting, and killing.

Warriors infected by the Silver Star's egg, many of them I had defeated. And exactly the same number of people who had stood beside me, I had killed.

Good and evil cancel each other out.

This <ruby>law of massacre<rt>rule</rt></ruby> imposed on me had not yet come to its end. I still had to kill.

Whom to kill next? Whom to make enemy, whom to make ally, and then cut down both?

The enemy, I did not know: the Silver Star, or whoever had been entrusted with the last egg. The ally—the ally, I knew.

天の喧騒はしかし、どこか空虚で、憂鬱な思索へと
沈みたがる意識を引き止める役には立たなかった。
　話し相手になってくれる人もいない。

　署長は出勤中、<ruby>家宰<rt>かさい</rt></ruby>の牧村さんは繁忙である。
　村正も日課の銀星号捜索に出向いていていない。雨
は劒冑の探査機能を妨害するが、銀星号の<ruby>香気<rt>けはい</rt></ruby>を掴む
能力はまた別なので問題ないようだ。

　錆びを知らぬ劒冑は雨中の探索行も苦としないのだ
ろう。水滴を弾きながら暗い鎌倉を飛び回る蜘蛛の姿
の相棒を思って、俺は羨んだ。
　為すべき何事かがあれば、無為に悩まなくても済む。

　……戦ってきた。
　戦って、戦って、殺してきた。

　銀星号の〝卵〟に冒された武者を幾人となく斃した。
　そして同じ数だけ、俺の傍らにいたひとを殺した。

　善悪相殺。

　俺に課せられたこの<ruby>虐殺法<rt>ルール</rt></ruby>は、まだ終わりを迎えて
いない。
　まだ、殺さなくてはいけない。

　次は誰を殺すのか。
　誰を敵とし、誰を味方とし、その両方を斬り伏せる
のか。

　敵はわからない。銀星号か、それとも最後の〝卵〟
預けられた誰かか。
　味方は――味方は、わかっている。

en.html:
It will be her.
The girl who goes forward single-mindedly, seeking the right path.

That figure I admire. I envy it. Every meeting, every sight of her, the feeling only grows.

If it were allowed, I too would have wished to be like her.

Righteous.
Straight.
Moving ahead without a swerve—

A way of being that is no longer possible for me. One who has committed so many sins and errors can choose only a life tied to them, carrying the responsibility.

Ichijou Ayane, I think of from a distance, as something precious.


Therefore, I will end up killing.

When I have killed the next enemy,
her—

Alone in a gray room.
Sitting there all by myself, I think only of such things.

Should I too go out and search for the Silver Star?

Suddenly I sensed a person and looked out at the garden.

A stone statue stood there, watching me.

en.html:
For an instant I thought my gloomy thinking had summoned a phantom. No. The girl was real.

She was standing there, rooted to the spot. She said nothing. Her face showed nothing.

For me, a welcome visitor. Even so, I could not bring myself to call out. That ferocious gaze of hers, always fixed straight ahead, had gone into hiding, and something misty had taken its place. Those flat eyes reminded me of a stone Buddha.

A lifeless statue is, after all, struck out of the full force of the sculptor's passion; likewise behind her unmoving pupils there were waves, easy to see. Their true shape, however, I could not see.

This was an Ichijou I was seeing for the first time. Not even the one from our first meetings, who openly loathed me. And she too was looking at me as if seeing me for the first time.

Cold. Rain or season had nothing to do with it; something was freezing me.

Perhaps it was fear.

Of what? What was there to fear?

The girl, beaten by the icy rain, silently thrust out one arm. The gesture was like aiming a gun. In her hand she was gripping a scrap of paper.

陰鬱な思索が幻を呼んだのかと、刹那はそう考えた。
　――違う。少女は実在だ。

　少女はそこにいて、そこに立ち尽くしている。

　物も言わない。
　表情もない。

　俺にすれば、歓迎すべき来客だ。
　しかし、声を掛けるのが躊躇われた。

　彼女特有の、苛烈なまでに真っ直ぐ前方へと向けら
れる眼光が、今は影を潜め、どこか靄のかかったそれ
に取って代わられている。
　その平板な瞳が石仏を思わせた。

　無機質なる仏像がその実、彫師の情念の丈をもって
打ち上げられているのと同じく、少女の揺れぬ双眸の
奥にも波濤があるのは容易に窺える。
　だが、その実相が見えない。

　初めて目にする一条だった。出会って最初の頃の、
俺を露骨に嫌悪していた姿とも違う。
　そして彼女もまた、初めて見るかのような目を俺に
向けているのだった。

　肌寒い。
　雨とも季節柄とも関わりなく、何かに凍える。

　それは恐れであったのかもしれない。
　
　――何を？　何を恐れるのか？

　氷雨に打たれる少女は音もなく、片腕を突き出した。
　それは銃を突きつける挙措に似ていた。

　手の中に、紙切れを握っている。

en.html:
Together with Ichijou, I entered a cinema hall in Kita-Kamakura. Perhaps because of the weather, the place was nearly empty. For about two hours we watched a movie whose content seemed to be a watermelon and rubber boots boiled together in glue.

Soaked in a thoroughly vague feeling, we went to a nearby soba shop for a late lunch. Now we were sitting at one of its tables, face to face.

What had been the intention behind Ichijou's sudden invitation, I had not yet asked. I was curious, but I missed the chance. Rescue from gloomy solitude was welcome, true, and that was one reason. But the bigger reason was this: Ichijou today was somehow off, wrapped in an air that made a casual question hard to ask.

Even at this point, it was the same.

一条と連れ立って、北鎌倉の銀幕へ入り。
　天候のせいだろう、閑散としていた館内で二時間程、
スイカと長靴を接着剤で煮込んだような内容の映画を
鑑賞し。

　何とも曖昧な感慨に浸りつつ、遅い昼食をとるため
近場の蕎麦屋へ。
　今はその卓の一つで向かい合っている。

　一条の唐突な誘いにどんな意図があったのか、それ
はまだ訊いていない。
　関心はあったが、訊きそびれた。

　何であれ陰鬱な孤独からの救いは有難かったという
のも理由ではある。がそれ以上に、やはり今日の一条
はどこかおかしく、安直な問いかけを躊躇わせる空気
に包まれているのが大きかった。

　この時点においてもそうだ。

ｅｔｃ／蕎麦屋の娘２"Haan ji, order please?"
Kageaki"Ichijou, what will you take?"
Ichijou"Ah, yes. Um... is the chilled tanuki still going?"
ｅｔｃ／蕎麦屋の娘２"Still? Not 'still', madam. That anti-human item, we have never served in this shop. Never."
Ichijou"...Wait, wait. Kya matlab, anti-human?"
ｅｔｃ／蕎麦屋の娘２"Ji, madam?"
Kageaki"What are you saying, Ichijou?"
Ichijou"What... what?"
Kageaki"Dipping tempura scraps in cold soup and eating them・・・・・・・・・・・・・・. Yeh insaanon ke liye nahi hai—not an act permitted to mankind. Go back as far as Australopithecus; even there, absolutely not."

Kageaki"It was our graduation trip. With my friends, I went around the famous places of Kamakura."
Kageaki"We paid respects at the Five Mountains. At Hachimangu we played at assassinating Sanetomo... and then it was just the right time for lunch, so we entered the nearest soba shop. That is this one."
Kageaki"Actually, on that trip I had made one mistake. I carried very little money."
Kageaki"Others were different. It was a trip, after all, so they had brought extra pocket money. As if to taunt me—rather, it was to taunt me—they ordered expensive items one after another."
Kageaki"Even today I remember. KonagayaKonagaya had the yam-and-grated-radish soba. Ozaki the same. Andou, if I recall, ordered the special soba, large size."
Kageaki"Every one of them was a high-price item, over one hundred yen. My total possession was a hundred yen and some change. Of course, they knew."
Kageaki"Do you understand?"
Ichijou"…………N-no. I don't."

en.html:
Ichijou(I don't even know what I am being asked...)
Kageaki"They were challenging me. Himmat hai? Your entire fortune, spend it here—only then your pride is safe. That was their challenge."
Kageaki"Such superior smiles they were giving, I had to decide. One hundred twenty-five yen in the wallet. I checked. After that figure was confirmed, what hesitation could remain?"
Kageaki"Tanuki soba. Sixty yen. That was my order."
Ichijou(...Himmat nahin thi. So he DIDN'T have the nerve...)
Kageaki"When their soba arrived, they began eating with great relish. And to me, waiting for my tanuki soba, they offered words of pity. Only on the surface."
Kageaki"In humiliating the defeated, they were masters."
Ichijou"Were they really your friends? Those people?"
Kageaki"But they did not know that victory and defeat were fated to turn over in a short while."
Kageaki"The turning point came the moment my soba arrived."
Kageaki"One look, and it was clear. That everything had reversed was plain to anyone's eyes."
Kageaki"When we left the shop, Konagaya muttered that the fellow who ordered the cheapest thing had gone and eaten the best thing. Saala. Beside him, Ozaki was desperately trying to memorize where the shop was."
Kageaki"I was the winner."
Ichijou"…………. So, um. What kind of soba was it, finally?"
Kageaki"Hm. That is how these things are."
Ichijou"Sorry?"
ｅｔｃ／蕎麦屋の娘２"Here you are!"

そんなたぬき蕎麦は俺もここでしか食べたことがない。
　単に弾けさせるだけなら簡単そうに思えるが。

　味との兼ね合いが難しいのかもしれない。この店の
たぬきは活きの良い天かすと蕎麦との相性が抜群なの
だった。
　一条も満足そうにしている。

　これでいくらかでも口が軽くなれば良いのだが。

How things would go hereafter, nobody could tell. The great upheaval of the other day would contribute strongly in exactly the opposite direction to political stability—long-term assessment aside.

Pessimistically, the <ruby>outcome<rt>outcome</rt></ruby> might be that this shop would close again before it ever became busy.

別としても。

<ruby>帰趨<rt>きすう</rt></ruby>も有り得る。

I flinched. Perhaps it resembled the feeling of someone afraid of sharp points.
